topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: It frames the lecture subject, context, and perceived complexity without yet introducing substantive course material.

topics.label: Foundations and core principles of complement
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the general organization, nomenclature rules, and central molecular hub of the complement system.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the upstream recognition mechanisms and threshold requirements that trigger the complement cascade.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the downstream biological processes through which activated complement destroys pathogens and drives inflammation.

topics.label: Host cell regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the protective mechanisms and regulatory proteins that prevent complement from damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical presentations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It details how deficiencies across different complement cascade proteins lead to specific disease presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms and applications of protein A
topics.groupedBecause: It examines how microbes subvert complement activity to survive and how these microbial evasion proteins are utilized in laboratory and clinical settings.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It delivers the closing framing and indicates the subject of the upcoming lecture.
